note: Authored teaching scenario. Every observation, prediction and evidence record below was written for this exercise. None was produced by running image software, and nothing here supports a claim about how any real tool or forensic technique behaves.

tolerance.note: A scenario rule, not an empirically validated forensic tolerance. It is set for this exercise so that you can apply a stated threshold consistently. Two predictions that fall inside 15 KB of each other are indistinguishable on file size — meaning this evidence cannot separate them, not that the files are identical.

routes.label: Route A — resize once, save once
Route B — save, resize, save again
steps: Reopen that saved file and resize to 1200 x 800

evidenceMenu.item: Retained intermediate-file record from the working directory
evidenceMenu.result:
Working directory listing, retained

  2027-03-02  09:14  source-2400x1600.tif      11,240 KB
  2027-03-02  09:41  interim-2400x1600.jpg      1,903 KB
  2027-03-02  09:52  output-7-1200x800.jpg          148 KB

The listing is a file-system record. It records what existed and when, not
what operation produced it.
evidenceMenu.why: The listing records a JPEG at the full source dimensions, created before the 1200 x 800 output. Route A never saves a JPEG before resizing, so route A cannot produce this listing. It is excluded. This does not establish route B: any history that saved at full size before resizing would leave the same listing.

evidenceMenu.item: Transformation log excerpt for the output
evidenceMenu.result:
Transformation log, excerpt as retained

  09:52:14  resize  2400x1600 -> 1200x800  filter=lanczos
  09:52:14  encode  jpeg quality=78 subsampling=4:2:0

Earlier entries were not retained. The log begins at the resize.
evidenceMenu.why: The excerpt records the resize and the encode that followed it. It says nothing about whether anything was saved before the resize, which is the only operation the two routes disagree about. Asking for it is reasonable; it does not separate them.

evidenceMenu.item: Inspection report for the output at 400 per cent
evidenceMenu.result:
Inspection report, authored for this scenario

  Examined: output-7-1200x800.jpg at 400 per cent
  Recorded: blocking visible at 8-pixel boundaries throughout;
            no feature recorded that the examiner could attribute
            to one save rather than two.
  Conclusion recorded by the examiner: no distinguishable difference.

This is a written report supplied with the scenario. No images were
produced or examined to generate it.
evidenceMenu.why: The supplied report records no distinguishable difference. Note what that is and is not: it is one examiner's recorded finding in this scenario, not a demonstration that single and double saves are visually identical in general.

evidenceMenu.item: EXIF metadata dump for the output
evidenceMenu.unavailableBecause: No EXIF survives in the output, and no intermediate metadata was retained.
evidenceMenu.why: Listed because it is the first thing most people ask for. It is not available here, which is itself worth recording in your report.

evidenceMenu.item: Upload log from the service the output was distributed through
evidenceMenu.unavailableBecause: Not retained by the service, and the course has no account with it.
evidenceMenu.why: Would have been informative. It does not exist.

reveal.truth: Output 7 was produced by route B.
reveal.whyBothFit: Every field required to match exactly does match: dimensions, chroma subsampling and the absence of EXIF are identical under both routes. On file size, route A's prediction is 6 KB from the observation and route B's is 7 KB, both inside the 15 KB scenario rule. So the initial observations do not separate the routes.
reveal.whatResolvesIt: E1. The retained working-directory listing shows a full-size JPEG existing before the 1200 x 800 output. Route A resizes before its only save, so route A cannot produce that file, and route A is excluded.
reveal.whatDoesNot: E2 and E3 are both reasonable requests that fail to separate the routes. E2's excerpt begins at the resize and is silent on whether anything was saved earlier — the one operation the routes disagree about. E3 records no distinguishable difference. A student who chose either and reported the question as still open has done the week correctly.
reveal.limits: Excluding route A is not establishing route B. Any history that saved at full size before resizing would leave the same directory listing — a save at quality 85 then a resize, or a route through a third intermediate size. Two routes were proposed; the evidence supports the weaker claim, which is 'not route A, and consistent with route B'. Every record in this pack is authored, and none of it demonstrates the behaviour of real software.
